title: Adic formal smoothness over a field implies regular locality
statement: Let $k$ be a field and $A$ a commutative $k$-algebra which is Noetherian [def-weil-pbc-noetherian-ring] and local, with unique maximal ideal $\mathfrak m$. If $k\to A$ is formally smooth for the $\mathfrak m$-adic topology [def-weil-pbc-formally-smooth-adic], then $A$ is a regular local ring [def-weil-regular-scheme].

source.place: More on Algebra, Lemma Tag 07EI (lemma-fs-implies-regular), statement and proof, lines 9534–9589 in the locally read Stacks source

proof.text: Pass to the maximal-ideal-adic completion; Noetherianity and formal smoothness pass to it, and regularity descends by the completion criterion.

The comparison-map lemma gives a map from the complete ring to a finite-variable power-series ring over its residue field, mapping the maximal ideal onto the variables ideal and inducing a surjection on the quotient. The power-series ring is regular local of the indicated dimension.

Apply Mathlib surjective_of_mk_map_comp_surjective using completeness of the source and separatedness for the image ideal of the target. Mathlib ringKrullDim_le_of_surjective then gives spanFinrank(m) = dim(T) ≤ dim(B). The Mathlib regular-local criterion IsRegularLocalRing.of_spanFinrank_maximalIdeal_le supplies regularity (its converse dimension bound is built into that criterion).
